correctness.rationale: Coordinate rotations diagonalize a radial compression in the monomials; the eigenvalue on degree k is the stated beta quotient with N=k+d-1 and block dimension binom(k+d-1,d-1). With A=N+1 and a=-ic, the change of variable y=t/(1-t) gives exactly exp(ic) Gamma(A+alpha+1) U(A,-alpha,a)/Gamma(alpha+1) by the defining Laplace integral, first for Re(a)>0 and then by an Abel limit dominated by y^N(1+y)^(-N-alpha-2). Equations 13.8.11 and 10.40.2 of DLMF give a leading factor sqrt(pi) exp(a/2) a^((2alpha+1)/4) A^(-(2alpha+3)/4) exp(-2 sqrt(aA))/Gamma(A) for U. The complex arguments meet the sector hypotheses; A to N costs only a relative 1+o(1). The gamma normalization and exp(ic+a/2)=exp(ic/2) recover the claimed formula, including the phase and polynomial exponent. The frozen gamma-average derivation is consistent: on S in [N/2,2N], the normalized large-s integrand is bounded by a constant times exp(C|S-N|/sqrt(N)); the exact mgf gives uniform integrability. Off this interval, the bound |H_a(s)|<=Gamma(alpha+1) s^(-alpha-1) and gamma tails with shape shifted by alpha+1 give exponentially small unnormalized error, so they remain negligible after root-exponential normalization. The complex Gaussian correction is exp(a/2). Taking moduli gives -log|lambda_k|~sqrt(2|c| k), so eventual nonvanishing, all S_p, and the counting constant follow by summing degree-block dimensions between quadratic log thresholds; no monotonicity or distinctness of eigenvalues is required. The comparison with T_|phi|=I is exact. Independent finite replay: rotated-contour quadrature in /workspace/review_checks.py (chirp), at N=512,2048,8192 for three parameter pairs including both signs of c, gave final complex relative errors 0.00692, 0.01141 and 0.02047 or smaller; it supplements, not establishes, the asymptotic. Supplied script inspected, not executed.
